rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Game Play 2.1 Draft Plan Cards 2.2 Place Plan Cards 2.3 Carry out actions 3 End of the game and scoring 3.1 Score scale 4 Expresso expansion icons Overview You represent one of the 4 coffee companies that from plantation, drying, roasting and distribution try to create and control the best supply chain of coffee. Game Play The game is played over 8 rounds where each player simulates the flow of coffee beans (cubes) through 4 stages: A. Produce, B. Dry, C. Roast and D. Deliver. Each round is divided into 3 phases: Draft Plan Cards At the beginning of each round, players take turns choosing 1 from 3 Plan Cards. 1. If choosing a card with a coffee cup icon, the player must pay with a cube. 2. The player does not have to pay if the business area has 2 visible ship icons Place Plan Cards Each player adds the chosen card to their Business Area 1. At the beginning of the game, the Business Area has a default card with all action icons. 2. Each new card must always cover 2, 3 or 4 visible squares of the existing Business Area Tip for BGA interface: Click/tap on a highlighted square to move the card towards the middle before rotating it. Carry out actions Each player performs between 1 (minimum) and 8 (maximum) actions, according to the number of visible coffee cup icons in their business area. The 4 types of actions are: A. Produce - Add a matching colour cube to each coffee bean icon. B. Dry - The player takes all the cubes of one color from one or more bean squares and joins them in a dry square. C. Roast - The player takes all the cubes of one color from one or more dry squares and joins them on a roast square. D. Deliver - The players take all the cubes from all the roast squares they want to and deliver these either to one or more coffee shops in their business area or to their warehouse. If a 2-square coffee shop is partially hidden it is NOT available to accept a delivery. Cubes placed on a coffee shop square remain there until the end of the game, unless the coffee shop is partially or totally hidden (in this case the cubes are removed to the supply piles). Cubes in the warehouse cannot be used later to fulfil coffee shop deliveries. NOTE - All action squares must be empty to do the action. Each cluster of orthogonally adjacent squares act as single action point - each square of the cluster produces/dries/roasts one set of cubes of one colour. The round ends when all players have completed their actions. End of the game and scoring The game ends after all players have performed their actions of the 8th and final round. Players earn victory points for their fully supplied coffee shops and for the cubes stored in their warehouse as follows: a) The colour with the fewest cubes earns 2 victory points per cube (0 if no cubes are stored). b) The colour with the second fewest cubes earns 1 victory point per cube (0 if no cubes are stored). c) Only two colours of cubes score, even if these 2, or more, have the same number of cubes. The player with the most points is the winner. In the event of a tie, the winner is the player with more cubes on roast spaces. If the tie persists the player with the most cubes on dry spaces wins. Score scale 30-35 Very good 36-40 Extraordinary 41+ Good luck with that! Expresso expansion icons EXPRESSO: when doing a D action this square can receive a cube from among those that are being delivered. At the end of the game and before scoring, the cube in this square can be exchanged for a cube of any color from the general supply and added to the warehouse. No more than one cube can be placed in this square and once placed here the cube will remain there until the end of the game. LOTE: this square produces one cube of any type (color). NATA: if at the end of the game this square is orthogonally adjacent to a fully supplied coffee shop the victory points of the shop are added with the points of the “nata” cake; no more than one “nata” per coffee shop can be scored and the same “nata” can’t score twice. PLUS: this square produces 2 cubes of the depicted type instead of 1. Image of icons

[Rating: 2/10] Maybe I don't get it, but if you get the cards you want is luck. The kinda engine building does not work properly in my eyes and does not feel satisfying.

[Rating: 3/10] I wanted to like Cafe, but I feel like the card selection mechanism is inherently broken. On your turn, you select a card to buy. If you cannot buy any,  you remove a card of your choice and discard it. These cards provide extra actions and with only eight rounds, you never want to discard a card. Cards are usually free, but the issue comes with cards that provide extra actions, which cost one completed coffee. The majority of cards provide an extra action, which means most are not free. [Rating: 3/10] A small euro in the style of “Eight Minute Empire”, "Century: Spice Road" or games of the “Tiny Epic” series. The gameplay is simple and straightforward: gather resources, roast them, deliver, get points. The main trick with the placement of cards most likely borrowed from ”Smartphone Inc.”  The most frustrating thing is that I'm a big fan of coffee, but the theme in this game is not disclosed at all. What are the coffee beans of different colors? Sort, kind? It's unclear. Not a single line in the rules is devoted to it. You can play, but there is nothing outstanding in this game.

[Rating: 3/10] A cool spatial puzzle intersects with Euro actions and step programming. Right at the threshold where casual gamers could attempt it but not do that well on their initial game. Low interaction so didn't set my heart racing but did enjoy the spatial arrangement and 30ish minute playtime.

[Rating: 4/10] Disappointing. I bought the game because the Honshu-like mechanism looked good. However, the cards have too many blanks and ships, and I don't find the ships to be very useful unless you get a pair early in the game. It is very important to have 2 driers and/or roasters together for efficiency but getting the right card to do this is too dependent on luck. If they re-made the game with 6 items on every card and no ships I might try it again. In the meantime, I'll brew my own.
